a5318d0404da.title: Doctor evidence file is absent from main
a5318d0404da.observation: doctor/README.md requires evidence.json to be read first because it carries settled rulings and the open backlog, but the doctor directory on main contains only PROMPTS.md and README.md. The required runtime truth therefore cannot be consulted, making duplicate-safe diagnosis impossible.
a5318d0404da.proposal: Restore the job that writes doctor/evidence.json before the Doctor run, and make absence or staleness of that file a visible failing workflow condition rather than silent missing state.
a5318d0404da.evidence: doctor/README.md lines 15-18 and 24-26 define doctor/evidence.json as required runtime truth; opening the main-branch doctor directory on 2026-08-05 shows only doctor/PROMPTS.md and doctor/README.md.

2801098e02ce.title: Showrunner documentation still describes caller fail-open behavior
2801098e02ce.observation: The reviewer's module and function documentation says infrastructure failures are treated as ship by callers or that the caller fails open, while the shared publish gate explicitly fails closed whenever will_upload is true. The executable policy is safer than the stale description, but the contradiction makes future maintenance error-prone.
2801098e02ce.proposal: Update the reviewer documentation to state that review_video raises on infrastructure failure and shared/showrunner_gate.py decides fail-open only for previews and fail-closed for real publishing.
2801098e02ce.evidence: scripts/showrunner_review.py lines 1-18 and the review_video docstring describe skipped/errored reviews as ship or caller fail-open; shared/showrunner_gate.py lines 20-31 and decide() implement fail-closed behavior for publish runs.

cda65fc717ba.title: Publish gate accepts malformed non-block verdicts
cda65fc717ba.observation: decide() blocks only when verdict.verdict is exactly 'block' or when a publish verdict has score=None. A malformed verdict such as verdict='error' with a numeric score, or an unknown verdict token with a score, is treated as SHIP even though it is not an affirmative approval.
cda65fc717ba.proposal: Define and validate a strict verdict schema at the gate boundary. On publish runs, require verdict='ship', a valid bounded numeric score, complete hard-check data, and the expected rubric/version metadata; treat every unknown or malformed value as blocked.
cda65fc717ba.evidence: shared/showrunner_gate.py lines 83-95 append a reason only for the exact string 'block' and for score is None, then return blocked=bool(reasons); no branch requires an explicit 'ship' verdict or rejects unknown verdict values.

df9eeac8ee28.title: Reviewer and gate both own final ship/block semantics
df9eeac8ee28.observation: scripts/showrunner_review.py computes a final ship/block verdict from score and auto-fails, while shared/showrunner_gate.py separately interprets that verdict and adds publish-context rules. Both files describe themselves as the decisive authority, leaving the final contract distributed across two modules and increasing the chance that new verdict states or stronger checks are added to only one layer.
df9eeac8ee28.proposal: Move the complete typed decision model into one canonical gate domain module: the reviewer should return measurements and anchored judgments, and one policy function should compute the only final disposition, including quality, infrastructure, publish context, schema validity, and ledger durability.
df9eeac8ee28.evidence: scripts/showrunner_review.py defines decide_verdict() as the single ship/block rule near lines 85-89; shared/showrunner_gate.py lines 1-31 and 47-95 describe and implement the whole fail-closed policy as a second decision layer.

6be0849a55e4.title: Cache hits bypass the recent-use penalty
6be0849a55e4.observation: On a cache miss, _prefilter subtracts media_usage.penalty(url) for assets used in the last 14 days. On a cache hit, search() rebuilds Candidate objects from cached dictionaries and returns immediately, so the current usage ledger is never consulted.
6be0849a55e4.proposal: Cache raw candidate facts, then rerun dynamic scoring on every read. Add a regression test that caches a URL, records it as used, and verifies that the next cache hit lowers its rank.
6be0849a55e4.evidence: funnel/media_funnel.py lines 1460-1472 apply media_usage.penalty() only inside _prefilter; lines 1572-1587 return cached candidates directly; funnel/media_usage.py lines 49-63 define the live 14-day penalty lookup.

3cca8a711ec4.title: Cached scores are not recomputed
3cca8a711ec4.observation: _cache_put stores Candidate.to_dict(), including the final score after time-dependent freshness, staleness, recent-use, same-host, and LLM adjustments. Cache hits restore that score unchanged for up to 48 hours.
3cca8a711ec4.proposal: Persist only source facts in the cache and recompute derived score components after every read, or store score components separately with explicit timestamps and invalidation rules.
3cca8a711ec4.evidence: funnel/media_funnel.py lines 145-154 include score in Candidate.to_dict(); lines 181-193 persist those dictionaries; lines 1475-1513 add dynamic score adjustments; lines 1572-1587 restore and return cached scores; CACHE_TTL_SEC is 48 hours at lines 105-107.

e02d4cf673bd.title: Timed-out providers lack terminal outcomes
e02d4cf673bd.observation: search() stops collecting after a 15-second timeout and calls shutdown(wait=False, cancel_futures=True). Already-running provider calls continue, can still update shared quota state, and have no run-scoped completed, cancelled, or timed-out record.
e02d4cf673bd.proposal: Add a structured provider outcome ledger and per-provider deadline handling so every started provider reaches a recorded terminal state before the search result is finalized, while preserving the overall latency limit.
e02d4cf673bd.evidence: funnel/media_funnel.py lines 1596-1632 stop result collection after 15 seconds and use shutdown(wait=False, cancel_futures=True); lines 196-241 update shared quota state from provider calls.

4c58349192b8.title: Asset metadata is assigned by provider class
4c58349192b8.observation: Candidate exposes source_class and license as asset metadata, but _prefilter assigns many values from a provider-name map rather than from item-level fields returned for the selected asset. Some stored values explicitly say verification is still required.
4c58349192b8.proposal: Move to a provenance-first asset manifest that stores source page, creator, original rights text, retrieval time, selection reason, and verification status for each chosen asset. Require item-level evidence for any lane that depends on it.
4c58349192b8.evidence: funnel/media_funnel.py lines 141-148 define source_class and license fields; lines 1420-1458 assign those fields from provider categories and include values such as 'verify per item'.

653acb99b575.title: Third-capture QA passes clips when QA itself crashes
653acb99b575.observation: The full review gate promises NEVER to raise, but its outer exception handler appends 'qa internal error (failed open)' and then sets verdict='pass'. Any unexpected probe, contact-sheet, vision, or local QA failure inside that try block therefore authorizes the clip instead of withholding it.
653acb99b575.proposal: Fail closed on QA-internal errors: return verdict='fail' (or an explicit quarantine/error verdict that every caller treats as non-publishable), preserve the exception text as evidence, and add a regression test that forces an internal QA exception and proves the clip cannot advance.
653acb99b575.evidence: third_capture/clip_qa.py, review(): the docstring says 'QA-internal error fails open'; the outer except appends 'qa internal error (failed open)' and assigns verdict = 'pass'.

75af24a46374.title: Dropping an overlength replay leaves its whoosh cue behind
75af24a46374.observation: build_edl() adds a 'whoosh' SFX cue at the start of an appended replay. If the output exceeds 52 seconds, it removes replay segments but filters cues only where cue[1] != 'riser'. The replay never added a riser, so its whoosh survives after the replay segment is gone and can fire at the old end-of-timeline position.
75af24a46374.proposal: When removing replay segments, remove the cue(s) owned by that replay using the replay start time or explicit cue ownership instead of filtering the unrelated 'riser' label; add a unit test for an over-cap EDL with replay enabled.
75af24a46374.evidence: third_capture/auto_edit.py, build_edl(): the replay branch appends (out_t, 'whoosh'); the subsequent max_out cleanup deletes kind=='replay' segments but removes only cues whose label is 'riser'.

cf263a770061.title: Hard novelty gate treats probe failure as a clean video
cf263a770061.observation: DIRECTOR.md defines NOVELTY as gate 0, says it is enforced rather than advised, and says a stale span rejects the render. novelty_check() obtains duration with ffprobe inside a broad exception handler, but on any exception it returns an empty list. Empty means no stale spans, so a broken/missing probe silently satisfies the hard gate.
cf263a770061.proposal: Represent 'could not evaluate novelty' separately from 'no novelty violations' and make the director fail closed when gate 0 cannot run. Persist the probe failure in the scorecard/report so a tooling outage is distinguishable from a genuinely clean film, with a test that forces ffprobe failure.
cf263a770061.evidence: data_learning/DIRECTOR.md, 'The hardline rule' and scorecard gate 0 require novelty enforcement; scripts/no_dull_beats.py, novelty_check(), catches any duration-probe exception and immediately returns [].

79e94e61b5a9.title: Proof-mode ledger is evidence without an integrity boundary
79e94e61b5a9.observation: capture_cli.py describes itself as the truthfulness layer whose replay and measured claims come from recorded artifacts. It hashes files that callers explicitly record, but the displayed shell_line is accepted directly from the caller, and save_ledger()/load_ledger() simply serialize and deserialize ordinary JSON. Nothing in this module binds argv, terminal events, shell_line, measurements, and referenced file hashes into one identity that a downstream renderer can verify before replay.
79e94e61b5a9.proposal: Evolve proof mode toward a content-addressed proof manifest: derive or validate the displayed command from argv, hash a canonical ledger payload containing argv/events/measurements/artifact hashes, and require downstream composition to verify that identity before treating a capture as proof. Keep human-readable JSON, but make tampering or accidental post-capture edits detectable rather than trusted by convention.
79e94e61b5a9.evidence: third_capture/capture_cli.py: capture() stores shell_line as shell_line or ' '.join(argv); record_file() hashes selected files; save_ledger() writes json.dumps(asdict(cap)); load_ledger() only json.loads() the file with no ledger-integrity verification.
